headline: GLOBAL GOLD ETFs PULL $18 BILLION IN AUGUST — EUROPE POSTS BIGGEST-EVER MONTHLY INFLOW AS HOLDINGS HIT RECORD 4,189 TONNES
snippet: World Gold Council data released September 10 shows global gold ETFs attracted $18 billion in August 2026 — the second-largest monthly inflow ever by value — lifting total holdings to a record 4,189 tonnes and AUM to $615 billion. European-listed funds posted their largest-ever monthly inflow at $7.9 billion; North American funds added $7.7 billion; Asian funds contributed $2 billion as Chinese, Indian and Japanese investor appetite accelerated. The sheer scale of institutional accumulation demonstrates that the Fed-rate-hike selloff in spot gold is not deterring wholesale repositioning from the world's largest fund managers.

headline: COPPER'S REAL DRIVER ISN'T TARIFFS — AI DATA CENTERS WILL CONSUME 475,000 MT OF THE METAL IN 2026, J.P. MORGAN SAYS
snippet: CNN Business analysis published September 10 lays out the structural copper demand case: a single large AI data center requires up to 50,000 metric tonnes of copper in electrical, cooling and distribution systems, and J.P. Morgan projects data centers alone will consume 475,000 MT in 2026. Meanwhile global copper mine output fell 1.1% in H1 2026 per ICSG, with Chile — the world's largest producer — down 6.6%. S&P Global models a potential 10-million-tonne annual shortfall by 2040 as demand targets 42 million tonnes against current 28 million tonne supply — making tariff uncertainty a sideshow compared to the structural copper deficit building beneath it.

headline: ARAFURA BREAKS GROUND ON NOLANS — AUSTRALIA'S FIRST INTEGRATED RARE EARTH PROJECT BEGINS CONSTRUCTION, A$1.6B BUDGET, FIRST NDPR IN 2029
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) has mobilized earthmoving equipment to the Nolans site in the Northern Territory — the first fully integrated ore-to-oxide rare earth operation in Australia — targeting 4,440 metric tonnes of NdPr oxide per year over a 38-year mine life. The A$1.6 billion project is financed by a multi-sovereign export credit agency syndicate (US, Canada, Germany, South Korea) alongside NAIF and Hancock Prospecting (15.5% equity), with Hatch appointed as EPCM contractor. First production of NdPr oxide is targeted mid-2029, adding meaningful non-China NdPr supply at scale to a market where China controls over 90% of current refining.

headline: GOLD X2 HITS 173M AT 0.89 g/t AU BENEATH MOSS PIT — RESOURCE NOW 2.46M OZ INDICATED, 4.21M OZ INFERRED IN NORTHWEST ONTARIO
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSXV: AUXX) released new assays September 10 from the QES Deeps resource expansion drilling at the Moss Gold Project in Northwest Ontario: hole MQD-26-474 returned 173.0m at 0.89 g/t Au from 685m depth, including 42.0m at 1.43 g/t Au — confirming bulk-tonnage grade continuity 100m below the existing pit design. With 12 of 21 planned QES expansion holes complete, the total Moss resource now stands at 2.458 million ounces indicated (1.04 g/t) and 4.209 million ounces inferred (0.97 g/t), building steadily toward a tier-two-scale open-pit gold deposit.

headline: TECTONIC METALS EXTENDS FLAT GOLD RIRGS TO 300M DEPTH — 30M AT 1.40 g/t AU IN ALASKA, MAIDEN RESOURCE ESTIMATE TARGETED Q1 2027
snippet: Tectonic Metals (TSXV: TECT) released the first 2026 assays from its Chicken Mountain drill program at the Flat Gold Project in southwest Alaska September 10: 30.00m at 1.40 g/t Au including 4.50m at 4.58 g/t Au, extending the higher-grade corridor to 300m vertical depth across 15 holes totalling 2,276m. Results confirm Chicken Mountain as a bulk-tonnage Reduced Intrusion Related Gold System (RIRGS) with heap-leach potential — one of six district-scale intrusion targets on the property — and a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate is now targeted for Q1 2027.

headline: AMERICAN PACIFIC DRILLS 20.1M AT 11.15 g/t AU IN MONTANA MASSIVE SULFIDE — HIGH-GRADE VMS OPEN DOWN-DIP AT MADISON
snippet: American Pacific Mining (CSE: USGD) reported September 9 that hole M26C-02 at the Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana intersected 30.8m of massive sulfide averaging 7.4 g/t Au, including 20.1m at 11.15 g/t Au, 14.3 g/t Ag and 0.42% Cu — with a high-grade sub-interval of 7.92m at 25.33 g/t Au and 0.86% Cu. The 15,000m 2026 program targets both shallow high-grade extensions and deeper porphyry targets; the system remains open down dip and to the southwest, with additional assays from the ongoing campaign pending.

headline: SUN PEAK DRILLS 39M AT 1.38% CU IN MAIDEN SAUDI ARABIA VMS PROGRAM — ARABIAN-NUBIAN SHIELD SYSTEM CONFIRMED AT SAFRA
snippet: Sun Peak Metals Corp. (TSXV: PEAK) released September 8 the first results from its 1,242m maiden drill program at the 100%-owned Safra VMS Project in the Nuqrah belt, 185km northeast of Medina in Saudi Arabia: 39.0m at 1.38% Cu and 0.84% Zn, plus a second interval of 19.42m at 1.17% Cu, 2.59% Zn and 22.35 g/t Ag. All seven holes at the Safra Main target returned mineralized intervals, confirming the surface VMS expression continues at depth across the 93km² licence area — an emerging copper-zinc district in a jurisdiction that has actively courted junior mining investment under Vision 2030.

headline: COPPER SMELTER FEES HIT $0 FOR FIRST TIME EVER — CHINA'S 50% GRIP ON GLOBAL REFINING CAPACITY BECOMES A STATECRAFT LEVER
snippet: Drawing on IEA data, a Eurasia Review analysis published September 8 documents how benchmark copper treatment charges (TC/RCs) fell to $0 per tonne in 2026 — the lowest on record — while spot TCs have been negative since 2024. China has expanded from 15% to 50% of global smelting capacity since 2005; non-Chinese smelter utilization has fallen below 70%. China agreed to cut production by 10% and halted 2 million tonnes of planned new capacity — but the analysis argues that this barely masks a structural dominance that now gives Beijing de facto pricing control over refined copper midstream, turning smelter economics into a geopolitical instrument.

headline: GOLD MINERS POSTED THEIR SECOND-BEST QUARTER EVER — YET TRADE AT 20X EARNINGS, CHEAPEST IN A DECADE
snippet: Investing.com analysis documents what may be the sector's widest valuation anomaly in a generation: gold miners recorded their second-best quarter ever in Q2 2026 — implied unit profits of $2,787/oz, up 50% year-over-year — yet the GDX top 25 now trade at just 20.2x TTM P/E, a compression of nearly 60% from Q4'23's 49.6x. The market is pricing an unlikely gold collapse; the companies are printing near-record earnings for a twelfth consecutive quarter. The author argues this divergence — record profits, decade-low valuation multiples — represents a structural entry point for investors willing to look past Fed-meeting noise.

headline: CANALASKA URANIUM MOBILIZES FOR FALL ATHABASCA DRILL — 6-10 HOLES AT KEY EXTENSION, 250M FROM THE PIKE ZONE DISCOVERY
snippet: CanAlaska Uranium (TSXV: CVV) has launched its 2026 fall diamond drill program at the Key Extension uranium project in the southeastern Athabasca Basin, Saskatchewan — 250 metres from the company's own West McArthur Pike Zone discovery, where previous drilling returned 3.10% uranium. The 6-10 hole program targets basement-hosted mineralization defined by EM and gravity anomalies, as uranium spot holds near US$90/lb. CanAlaska is one of roughly two dozen juniors drilling approximately 100,000-110,000 metres across the Athabasca Basin in 2026, the most active exploration campaign the basin has seen in a decade.
